label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Here is a reply you can post as is:

---

Bonjour D. Bergeron, and bonjour everybody,

I read the whole thread, every message. You asked me for a straight answer and you are right to ask, so here it is. We are not closing. We are not moving. It is the opposite: I bought the building.

I wanted to keep it as a surprise for the reopening. I liked the idea of seeing your faces on the day. Then my nephew showed me this thread, and I think the surprise is finished! That was my mistake, I should have told you sooner. So I will tell you everything now, and I start with the carnets, because that is what matters most to the people who paid.

I see how the timing looked. Carnets in October, a closed sign in December. But a bakery that plans to disappear does not order a new oven. We sold 214 carnets in October, $60 for 12 loaves. Every one of them is still good. There is no expiry date. noodle_and_crumb, if you have 7 loaves left today, you have 7 loaves left the day we reopen, and in the summer, and next year if you eat slowly. Also, every carnet holder gets one free croissant in January, once we are open again. Just show me your carnet.

And if somebody really prefers to have the money back, come to the shop and I will give it back. No questions, no hard feelings. You don't have to explain why.

I will say one thing about the word "scam" and then I leave it alone. I understand why people worry. Mile End has lost many small shops, and I have watched the same ones close as you. When you see a paper taped on a door, you think the worst. I would think the same. But I have been on this street since March 2009. Seventeen years. To read that word beside the name of my bakery, it hurt. I am not looking for a fight with anybody, and I prefer that people ask the question out loud. Now you have the answer.

Now the building. Marc-Antoine, your cousin is half right. The building was sold. It was sold to me!

The owner, M. Ferland, is 81 years old and he is retiring to Sherbrooke with his daughter. He offered to sell to me before anybody else, and we signed at the notary on December 15. Some of you know him without knowing it. He is the gentleman who has come in every morning for 17 years for his baguette "pas trop cuite". He cried a little at the notary. I will miss him at the counter.

So there will be no condos, no bank and no vape shop downstairs. The bakery stays at its corner on Fairmount. For a small shop, owning the walls changes everything. Nobody can sell the building over my head any more.

For the three apartments upstairs: I know that when a building is sold, the people living above are the first to be afraid, and with reason. They stay rented, same tenants, same rent. I promised it to them in writing already, and I repeat it here so the whole street knows. Nothing changes for you.

Why are we closed from January 4 to 18? For works. Two things.

The first is a new oven. A deck oven with 4 decks, coming from a supplier in Laval. The old one is from 1998 and it broke down three times this year. It deserves its retirement too.

The second is the space at the back, the old storage room of the dépanneur. We are taking it, and we will put 6 small tables there. After 17 years, people can finally sit down. You have been eating your croissants standing on the sidewalk long enough.

About the sign. My nephew Thomas wrote it at 6 in the morning. "Grande nouvelle" was his idea and I said ok without thinking. When I read it again with your eyes, I see the problem. A closed sign and a mystery together, of course people got nervous. That is my fault, not his.

And Jules, the half empty shelves have nothing to do with closing. We sold everything for Christmas Eve, 400 bûches. Your pain de campagne is safe.

So, the dates, for those who skipped to the bottom:

Closed from January 4 to January 18.

We reopen Tuesday, January 19, at 7 a.m.

Saturday, January 23, we celebrate the reopening and everybody is invited. Coffee and a piece of the new bread, free, carnet or no carnet. Come see the oven and try a table. Bring the neighbours.

Priya, thank you, and thank you to everybody else who defended us. Tell your kid the chocolatines are not going anywhere. And yes, bakers are allowed two weeks off. Maybe one day!

D. Bergeron, you wrote that a two-week vacation does not need a "big news soon". You are right, it is not a vacation. Thank you for asking me directly, I like it better that way. And if anybody wants to ask me something in person before the 4th, I am at the counter.

À bientôt, and see you on the 23rd.

Hélène Gagnon
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré

---

Two things to check before you post:

- **Saturday the 23rd:** I gave no hour for the celebration because you didn't give me one. Add it if you have one.
- **Before the 4th:** I wrote that people can come ask you at the counter before the 4th. Take that line out if you are not there every day over the holidays.
